nodes.description: A common inversion between the two olfactory receptor gene clusters at 8p23, carried heterozygously by the mother. This is a normal polymorphism, not a mutation - reported at 39% allele frequency in a Japanese population and 26% in Europeans - and it is curated as the first node because it is the substrate the rearrangement needs, not because it is pathogenic in itself.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular characterization of inv dup del(8p): analysis of five cases.
evidence.snippet: FISH analysis showed all their mothers to be heterozygous carriers of an 8p23 inversion [inv(8)(p23)].

evidence.reference_title: Molecular characterization of inv dup del(8p): analysis of five cases.
evidence.snippet: The frequency of the inv(8)(p23) allele is 39% in a normal Japanese population, comparable to 26% in Europeans

nodes.description: In a heterozygous carrier, the inverted segment and its normal counterpart pair as a loop at pachytene of meiosis I. Recombination within that loop generates the rearranged chromosome; the version with a homozygous duplication requires two recombinations, one inside the loop and one between the loop and the centromere. A subsequent rescue event removing part of the duplicated segment and one centromere is what leaves a viable chromosome.

nodes.description: The functional consequence is two dosage changes in opposite directions on one chromosome - monosomy for the distal segment and trisomy for the proximal one - so the phenotype is the sum of a loss and a gain rather than the effect of either. Duplication extent varies between patients, and the largest series used that variation to refine a 5.1 Mb region common to the duplications of patients with callosal anomalies.

The paper reporting it is explicit that this is atypical.

nodes.description: The product: one chromosome carrying a deleted distal segment, an intact segment in between, and a duplicated proximal segment in inverted orientation. In every patient analysed the proximal deletion breakpoint and one duplication breakpoint were the same position, each inside one of the 8p23 olfactory receptor clusters - which is what shows the two lesions are one event rather than two.

nodes.description: An immune component reported once and worth curating because it has a candidate mechanism on the deletion side. A one-month-old with invdupdel(8p) and severe respiratory syncytial virus bronchiolitis had reduced natural killer cell activity and reduced alpha-defensin against healthy controls; the defensin gene cluster sits at 8p23.1 and is inside the deleted segment. No frequency is asserted: the single report is a mechanistic one, and its own authors say cellular immune function has never previously been described in this syndrome, so there is no denominator to grade against.
